title: Price Alert Days
statement: A trading app has 2,000,000 daily closing prices. For every day it must show how many days later the price first goes higher (0 if never).

approaches.name: A monotonic stack of waiting day indexes; each new higher price answers the cheaper days on top
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Each day is pushed and popped once.

approaches.name: For each day, scan forward until a higher price
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but up to 2 trillion comparisons on a falling market.

approaches.name: Sort days by price and search later days
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Can be made to work with a balanced tree of indexes, but is harder and slower than the stack.

approaches.name: Compare each day with the overall highest price
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Gives whether a higher price exists, not how many days until the first one.

title: Shortest Voucher Code
statement: A shop prints 100,000-digit voucher numbers and must delete exactly 1,000 digits from each, keeping the order of the rest, so that the remaining number is as small as possible.

approaches.name: Scan the digits with a stack; while removals are left and the new digit is smaller than the top, pop
approaches.hint: Drop a bigger digit before a smaller one
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Each digit is pushed and popped at most once, and each pop makes an earlier position smaller.

approaches.name: Repeat k times: delete the first digit that is bigger than the next one
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Same result, but rescans the number for every deletion.

approaches.name: Delete the k largest digits
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Position matters more than size: in "10200" with k = 1, deleting the 2 leaves 1000, but deleting the 1 leaves 200.

approaches.name: Try every way to delete k digits
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Correct but impossible for these sizes.

title: Skyline Viewpoints
statement: A city has 500,000 buildings in a row facing a park on the right. The planning office needs, for every building, the first building to its right that is at least as tall, which blocks its view.

approaches.name: A monotonic stack of indexes still looking for a blocker
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Each building is pushed once and popped once, when its blocker arrives.

approaches.name: For each building, walk right until a building at least as tall
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but slow for a skyline that keeps rising.

approaches.name: Sort buildings by height first
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Loses the left-to-right order that the question is about.

approaches.name: Mark only the tallest building
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Says nothing about the blocker of every other building.
